column1: # Cache-owned relationships such as NPC idle/walk/turn
# SpotAnim sequenceId and interface animation IDs do NOT need to be duplicated
# here. This file is for gameplay/presentation relationships that vanilla 317
# expected the server/content layer to choose.
# Preserved RuneScript selected these from worn right-hand items. Source GFX
# are attached to the player. Ranged entries use one representative ElForge
# flight (MSB uses two) because the real server owns target/tick orchestration.
# Community-documented classic 317 gameplay mapping for NPC 941:
# Tier A: preserved RuneScript/config relationships (strong evidence).
# Temple of Ikov fire warrior: body cast + source casting GFX + travelling fire blast.
# Death Plateau troll throwers: troll_rock_throw + launch/travel rock GFX.
# Tree gnomes: bow attack + iron arrow launch/travel.
# Regicide elf warrior: human_bow + glowing arrow launch/travel.
# Horror from the Deep ranged Dagannoths: ranged body attack + spine projectile.
# Skeletal wyvern: melee body attack plus explicit fire-breath special.
# Tier B: reconstructed 2006-era combat projectile pairings.
# These come from NpcCombat behavior; use separate actions where the NPC has random attack variants.
# Spinolyps: magic and ranged projectile variants by NPC id.
# Ahrim representative magic variant: source GFX + projectile.
# Chaos Elemental two explicit projectile variants.
# TzTok-Jad: magic and ranged variants use different body sequences/projectiles.
# Dragon families: reconstructed server pairs the normal body attack with red fire-breath projectile.
# Green dragon 941 keeps the separately researched cast binding already present above.
# Tier C: broad NPC attack/defend/death coverage from the 2006Scape NpcEmotes table.
# Stronger Tier A rows above override/augment conflicting attack semantics.
# Existing authored NPC/action keys above this block always win.
# This broad source is lower-confidence than the hand-authored RuneScript/projectile rows.
# Columns after duration_ms are optional: variant
# placement: source | projectile | target. Projectile geometry uses classic RuneTek server values; existing rows remain valid.
